Sia Title: Project Consultant (Exempt Contractor)

Project Title: Senior Lifecycle & CRM Strategy Leader

Project Length: This is a contract role that could span 6 months with the possibility of extension

Project Hours: 40 hours per week

Location: Remote

Rate: $90-110/hr The expected compensation for this contract is per year. The exact pay rate will vary depending on a wide array of factors, which may include but are not limited to skills, experience, and location.

About the role

We’re seeking a senior lifecycle and CRM leader to build a coordinated customer-growth capability for a digital-presence services business serving entrepreneurs, small businesses, freelancers, and customers building and managing an online presence. The portfolio spans domain registration, website creation, web hosting, professional email, security, and digital marketing solutions.

The business is evolving from product- and campaign-led communications toward a more integrated lifecycle model. You will assess the current state, define the highest-value customer journeys, and establish a practical roadmap connecting customer and account data, setup and service signals, marketing technology, content, measurement, and cross-functional execution.

The work should help customers move from purchasing a domain or digital service to successfully establishing, activating, managing, protecting, and growing their online presence. It should strengthen service activation, time to value, complementary-service adoption, renewal readiness, retention, expansion, and win-back. You will serve as a senior advisor while remaining hands-on in shaping the first wave of journeys, tests, and operating practices.

What You’ll Do

  • Assess the end-to-end digital-presence lifecycle. Map the experience from domain search and purchase through account setup, website creation and launch, hosting and professional email activation, security adoption, ongoing management, renewal, cancellation or lapse, win-back, and expansion into relevant adjacent services.
  • Build the lifecycle strategy and roadmap. Define lifecycle stages, customer and business outcomes, journey priorities, and a sequenced plan balancing immediate improvements with longer-term data, technology, content, and operating-model needs.
  • Design high-value customer journeys. Develop coordinated programs for onboarding, service activation, website launch, customer education, renewal preparation, lapse prevention, retention, service recovery, win-back, and expansion into complementary digital-presence services.
  • Advance segmentation and trigger strategy. Define actionable audiences and triggers using customer profile, domain and service purchases, setup milestones, website launch status, account activity, billing and renewal status, support interactions, engagement, and service-portfolio signals.
  • Connect CRM, service, and channel data. Determine the data, identity, consent, automation, and integration capabilities required to coordinate experiences across email, web, account experiences, service interactions, and other available channels.
  • Improve personalization and next-best-action decisions. Deliver relevant setup guidance, website-launch support, education, security and renewal reminders, complementary-service recommendations, and re-engagement based on where customers are in building and managing their online presence.
  • Establish experimentation and measurement. Define baselines, test plans, controls, and reporting for setup completion, service activation, website launch, time to value, multi-service relationships, engagement, renewal, lapse prevention, retention, win-back, customer value, and incremental commercial impact.
  • Create the lifecycle operating model. Clarify decision rights, ownership, intake, prioritization, approvals, production, reporting, and optimization across marketing, product, ecommerce, customer care, data, analytics, creative, and technology.
  • Move the first wave into delivery. Translate recommendations into journey maps, briefs, audience and trigger definitions, content requirements, test designs, measurement plans, and a prioritized delivery backlog.
  • Build sustainable internal capability. Create reusable frameworks, governance, documentation, and working rhythms that enable internal teams to continuously improve lifecycle programs.

What Success Looks Like

  • A clear lifecycle and CRM maturity assessment covering journeys, data, segmentation, triggers, channels, technology, content, measurement, and team capability.
  • A prioritized roadmap tied to customers establishing, activating, managing, protecting, and growing their online presence, with measurable outcomes across time to value, renewal, retention, expansion, and win-back.
  • A defined first wave of journeys with owners, requirements, dependencies, tests, and measurement.
  • A more connected experience for customers holding one or multiple services across domains, websites, hosting, professional email, security, digital marketing, billing, renewals, and support.
  • Clear governance and operating rhythms across the functions supporting the customer experience.
  • Internal teams equipped to sustain and improve the lifecycle capability.
  • Approximately 15+ years across lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention, customer engagement, marketing automation, customer journey, or growth CRM.
  • Senior Director or VP-level experience advising executives and influencing cross-functional decisions.
  • Experience building a lifecycle capability from a low-maturity starting point, not only optimizing an established program.
  • Deep experience with recurring-revenue digital services, especially domain registration, web hosting, website building, professional email, online security, digital marketing, ecommerce enablement, or adjacent small-business services.
  • Ability to connect customer strategy with data, identity, consent, marketing technology, service signals, support interactions, content, execution, and measurement.
  • Experience designing journeys from purchase through setup, activation, launch, ongoing value realization, renewal, expansion, retention, service recovery, lapse prevention, and win-back.
  • Fluency in segmentation, event-based triggers, journey orchestration, personalization, experimentation, and incremental measurement.
  • Experience managing lifecycle complexity across customers who may own a single service or a portfolio of interconnected digital-presence services.
  • Ability to balance executive counsel with hands-on development of journey maps, briefs, audience definitions, test plans, roadmaps, and operating processes.
  • Availability for a fully remote, full-time contract engagement aligned to Pacific Time working hours.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout their employment. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Sia is a next-generation, global management consulting group. Founded in 1999, we were born digital. Today our strategy and management capabilities are augmented by data science, enhanced by creativity and driven by responsibility. We’re optimists for change and we help clients initiate, navigate and benefit from transformation. We believe optimism is a force multiplier, helping clients to mitigate downside and maximize opportunity. With expertise across a broad range of sectors and services, our 3,000 consultants serve clients worldwide from 48 locations in 19 countries. Our expertise delivers results. Our optimism transforms outcomes.

Sia Experience is the end-to-end marketing and customer experience arm of Sia. Agile and collaborative, our Marketing AdvisoryBusiness Line is recognized for delivering high-impact, growth-focused solutions by blending marketing, CX, creative, AI, and deep industry expertise.

As strategic partners, The Marketing Advisory team empowers clients across technology, luxury, consumer goods, finance, energy, and more to scale operational excellence and drive brand-led growth through AI- and data-driven strategies. Our teams lead full-funnel marketing transformations—from strategy and go-to-market execution to experience design, performance measurement, and sustainable impact.

It’s an exciting time to join us. SiaX has long been the agency behind some of the world’s biggest brands—now we’re expanding, becoming one of the most recognizable names for companies that demand bold, business-driving creative. We’re shaping SiaX into the go-to agency of the future. This is your chance to be part of that growth, working alongside top-tier creatives, consultants and agency leaders to continuously evolve what a modern, full-service agency can be. Opportunities like this don’t come around often—if you want in on the next level, this is it.

About us

Ann Taylor embodies and celebrates the spirit, heritage, and confidence of American women leading the lives they love. Since its beginnings, Ann Taylor has been committed to providing women with everything they need to feel inspired and motivated as they navigate their multifaceted lives. Our effortlessly polished styles are thoughtfully designed to go anywhere—from the office to special occasions (and everywhere in between).Discover a culture centered on empowering employees, with access to industry leaders and tools you need to expand your skills and stretch your abilities. We'll meet you at every milestone with opportunities and benefits to make life better in and outside of work (not to mention your closet). Ready to join us?

About the role

The Copywriter is responsible for the concept, development, and implementation of creative, seasonal, and promotional copy for Ann Taylor Marketing. The Copywriter understands the brand positioning and voice to be able to express each season's important fashion/cultural trends in a compelling, original, elevated, and accessible way to keep Ann Taylor’s

consumer-facing communication modern, relevant, differentiated, and inspired. The Copywriter understands how to leverage consumer insights and seasonal mindset while also working at a fast pace to address needs as they come up. They also understand how to adapt voice based on channel (e.g. social, email, paid media, etc.) and audience type (e.g. acquisition, retention, reactivation, etc.) while still being brand-appropriate. The right candidate understands the balance of communicating the brand’s values and promoting brand awareness while understanding the importance of supporting the business through driving traffic and sales to our stores and website.

Where do you belong?

Your career is more than just a job, it's part of your life. Whether you’re a clinician, or non-clinical professional, at USACS you'll feel a sense of connection working with clinicians and office staff who share your interests and values. We want you to love coming to work each day because you believe in what you do and the people with whom you work. We care about your success.

USACS also understands that location is important. We offer career opportunities for clinicians and non-clinical support staff from New York to Hawaii and numerous points in between. Our supportive culture, outstanding benefits and competitive compensation package is best in class.

Job Description

The Director, Coding Quality Assurance – Inpatient and Emergency Medicine, provides leadership to the Coding Quality Assurance Inpatient and Emergency teams by establishing tools, workflows, SOPs, policies, and procedures to ensure consistency across all coding organizations. The Director monitors coding quality results to ensure the quality and production of work by USACS coders, and vendor partner coders maintain Coding Quality Assurance Programs (CQAP) across multiple specialties. This role is also accountable for developing and maintaining a process to identify risk and partners with clinicians, coding education, and operations to ensure quality scores exceed industry expectations.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

Visioning, Strategic Leadership, & Planning – 50%

  • Develop and execute the strategic direction for the Coding Quality Assurance Inpatient and Emergency teams.
  • Establish and maintain QA frameworks, policies, workflows, and SOPs to ensure consistency in coding practices.
  • Monitor coding accuracy trends and performance metrics to identify risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Partner with coding operations, coding education, and clinical leadership to ensure coding quality performance meets organizational and industry benchmarks.
  • Collaborate with coding vendor partners to promote consistency in processes.
  • Develop quality performance goals, benchmarks, and tools to support quality improvement.
  • Identify emerging trends impacting coding quality and implement proactive strategies.

Quality and Operational Oversight – 25%

  • Oversee the Coding QA program, including auditing processes.
  • Monitor QA scores for internal and external coders by specialty. Provide feedback to education and operation teams to establish action plans.
  • Ensure the integrity and reliability of coding quality metrics and reporting.
  • Identify and recommend initiatives and programs for coding quality improvements.
  • Identify any potential coding quality risk and initiate remediation plan which may require continuous monitoring and evaluation.
  • Collaborate with coding operations and education teams to address discrepancies and identify gaps.
  • Evaluate trends to identify training opportunities and operational improvements.

Shaping Team Culture & Development – 15%

  • Provide leadership and direction to the Coding Quality Assurance team.
  • Recruit, develop, and mentor QA staff promoting a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Conduct regular performance discussions, coaching, and development planning.
  • Sets a positive example in collaborating initiatives, identifying solutions, measuring, and sharing results, and providing feedback.

Professional Development – 10%

  • Maintain expertise in coding standards, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
  • Participate in continuing education, professional development, and industry forums.
  • Serve as a mentor and resource for staff and emerging coding professionals.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Strong knowledge of medical coding principles, regulatory requirements, and compliance standards.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience managing coding quality assurance programs.
  • Ability to analyze coding quality data and translate findings into actionable improvement initiatives.
  • Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills across multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills.
  • Proven ability to lead continuous improvement initiatives and manage performance metrics.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, with emphasis on Excel.
  • Ability to identify, research and solve problems and discrepancies.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Associate degree required; Bachelor’s or Master’s degree preferred.
  • RHIT, RHIA, CCS-P, CPC or other job-related certification required.
  • 6+ years’ coding experience and leadership/supervision experience required.
  • 6+ years of relevant experience managing coding inventory across a large physician practice or multi-site healthcare organization with high accountability for quality and production metrics.
  • 6+ years of relevant experience managing HIM/Coding workflow and data capture processes, including within an electronic medical records system.
  • 6+ years of relevant experience in managing multiple, large coding teams and/or projects, and influencing senior-level management and key stakeholders.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for prolonged periods and occasionally walk, stand, bend, stoop, and lift up to 15 pounds.
  • Required to have close visual acuity to perform the job.

Salary Range:

$103,887.00 - $192,191.00

Salary may be determined on several factors including but not limited to knowledge, skills, experience, education, geographical location and requirements stated in job description.

USACS offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees.

Benefits may vary based on role, location, and employment status, but generally include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance options

  • Health savings accounts (HSA) and flexible spending accounts (FSA)

  • 401(k) employee and employer contributions

  • Paid time off, including vacation, sick leave, and company holidays

  • Paid parental leave & family support benefits

  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance

  • Employee assistance programs & wellness resources

Additional compensation may include bonus eligibility, equity, or other incentive programs, depending on the role.

Specific benefit offerings and eligibility will be provided during the hiring process and may be subject to change in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

raw.excerpt: Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners.
raw.description:
Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners.
We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.
Since launching publicly in September 2023, Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue, with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue)—the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
- Mission-critical problems: We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.
- High bar, low ego: Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.
- Speed over comfort: We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.
- Enduring impact: What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.

Team & Locations

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

Flex Fuels Ambition.

About the role

Flex moves real money at a serious scale, and someone has to make sure it only moves for the right reasons. We're hiring our first Financial Crimes Analysts to be that someone, and to build the function around them.

This is a net-new role. You'll report directly to the Head of Financial Crimes and work side by side with the people who designed our financial crime program. Once a customer is through the door, you own what happens next: monitoring their activity, investigating what looks wrong, deciding what is suspicious, and writing the narrative that backs the decision.

Your first priority will be working through our alert and case backlog and keeping the queue moving, which means a lot of hands-on investigation from day one. Our processes are still being built, so you'll also notice what's clunky, document it, and help simplify it. As the backlog comes under control, you'll have more room for bigger improvements. The scope is broader than a typical analyst role because the function is still taking shape, and the people who join first will set its standards and its reputation with our partners.

This is a strong fit if you have a few years of hands-on financial crimes experience, enjoy digging into cases, and want to grow from running a process into helping design one, with a clear path into broader program responsibilities as the team grows.

What you'll own

You'll be a core part of financial crime detection and investigation at Flex.

  • Post-onboarding risk. Own the question "is this customer's activity legitimate?" from the moment an alert fires to the moment it is cleared, escalated, or filed.

  • The queue and the backlog. Your first priority is working through our alert backlog and keeping the queue current, with an eye on both quality and speed, so real risk gets the scrutiny it deserves and good customers aren't slowed down by noise.

  • The investigation standard. Help set the bar for what a strong case narrative looks like here: clear, well supported, and defensible to a regulator or bank partner without a follow-up call.

  • Detection coverage. Flag the typologies, patterns, and blind spots you see across cases and bring them to Risk, Operations, and Engineering, so they can become better rules and fewer false positives.

  • The process. Document what works and flag what's clunky as you go. As the backlog comes under control, you'll have room to take on bigger improvements.

  • Your voice. As one of the first official Financial Crimes Analysts at Flex, you'll see where the process works and where it doesn't, and you'll have a real voice in how the team grows.

What you'll do

Detect and decide

  • Review and disposition transaction monitoring alerts, applying BSA/AML typologies to separate genuinely suspicious activity from false positives

  • Investigate unusual activity across accounts, payments, and cards, including patterns that point to money laundering, fraud, account takeover, and other illicit behavior

  • Escalate higher-risk cases to supervisory review with a clear recommendation, not just a pile of facts

  • Support UAR and SAR filings, working alongside senior team members and building toward owning filings end to end

Investigate and document

  • Write case narratives so clear and well supported that a reviewer, examiner, or bank partner can follow your reasoning without a call

  • Conduct enhanced due diligence on existing customers whose activity raises concerns, and refresh customer risk profiles when behavior no longer matches what we were told at onboarding

  • Pick up cases handed over by our KYC team when a flagged account needs a deeper activity review, and hand back what you learn so onboarding decisions get sharper

  • Keep accurate, complete records in our case management system

Build the program

  • Help flag the patterns and process gaps behind noisy alerts or missed risk, and help turn them into better detection rules and simpler procedures

  • Partner with Risk, Operations, Support, and Engineering to close open requests and, over time, tune monitoring

  • Support quality assurance and file reviews, including for our bank partner program

  • Stay current on evolving AML typologies and regulatory guidance, and bring what you learn back to the team

What we're looking for

You're comfortable with ambiguity, you make sound calls with incomplete information, and you can work a high-volume queue without losing quality.

You have

  • 1–3 years in BSA/AML compliance, transaction monitoring, fraud operations, or a related financial crimes role

  • Hands-on experience dispositioning transaction monitoring alerts in a platform such as Sardine, Unit21, Actimize, or similar, with a working knowledge of AML typologies

  • Exposure to fintech, payments, card programs, or BaaS program compliance

  • Experience tuning detection rules or working with data and SQL to investigate patterns

  • Working knowledge of KYC/CDD requirements and BSA obligations

  • Exposure to suspicious activity reporting, including drafting narratives or supporting UAR/SAR filings

  • Strong written communication: you can explain why something is or isn’t suspicious in plain language and summarize complex findings concisely

  • High attention to detail, plus the ability to manage a queue and prioritize well

  • A self-driven, growth mindset: you don’t wait to be handed the next problem, and when you see a clunky step or a noisy rule, you fix it and write down the better way

Bonus points

  • CAMS or another AML certification, completed or in progress

Why Join Us

Build something generational — Capture the full lifecycle of money for ambitious business owners.
Work on real money, real risk — Payments, credit, and banking at serious scale.
Solve hard problems — AI, underwriting, compliance, and global finance from first principles.
True ownership — Small teams, high trust, real accountability.
Founder-level exposure — Direct access to leadership, customers, and investors.
High bar, high taste — Move fast without cutting corners.
Elite peers — People here are builders, not tourists.
Real upside — Meaningful equity if you help build something big.

Position Summary

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.

The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Risk Management

  • Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.
  • Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.
  • Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.
  • Provide independent oversight of business decisions and strategic initiatives.
  • Promote a strong risk culture throughout the organization.

Credit Risk Management

  • Oversee retail credit portfolios, including:
    • Mortgages
    • Personal Loans
    • Credit Cards
    • Auto Loans
    • Consumer Finance Products
  • Establish underwriting standards and credit policies.
  • Monitor portfolio quality, delinquency trends, and loss performance.
  • Lead stress testing and credit risk scenario analyses.
  • Recommend risk-adjusted lending strategies.

Operational Risk Management

  • Develop frameworks to identify and manage operational risks.
  • Monitor operational incidents, control failures, and emerging risks.
  • Oversee business continuity and operational resilience programs.
  • Strengthen internal controls and risk reporting mechanisms.
  • Ensure effective risk and control self-assessment processes.

Regulatory Compliance & Conduct Risk

  • Ensure compliance with banking regulations and consumer protection laws.
  • Oversee conduct risk management and fair customer treatment initiatives.
  • Maintain strong relationships with regulatory authorities.
  • Lead regulatory examinations and risk-related audits.
  • Ensure implementation of regulatory changes and risk controls.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk

  • Oversee fraud prevention, detection, and investigation programs.
  • Strengthen anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing controls.
  • Monitor financial crime risks and emerging threats.
  • Ensure effective transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting.
  • Collaborate with law enforcement and regulatory agencies when necessary.

Market & Liquidity Risk Oversight

  • Monitor interest rate risk and liquidity risk exposures.
  • Evaluate balance sheet vulnerabilities and stress scenarios.
  • Support asset-liability management activities.
  • Ensure adherence to regulatory capital and liquidity requirements.

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

  • Oversee technology and cyber risk governance.
  • Assess cybersecurity threats and resilience capabilities.
  • Ensure robust controls for digital banking platforms.
  • Monitor third-party and vendor risk exposures.
  • Support digital transformation initiatives through effective risk management.

Governance & Reporting

  • Present risk reports to Executive Management, Risk Committees, and the Board.
  • Develop key risk indicators (KRIs) and risk dashboards.
  • Ensure timely escalation of significant risk issues.
  • Maintain effective risk governance structures and committee frameworks.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Lead risk management teams across multiple disciplines.
  • Develop future risk leaders and succession plans.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and transparency.
  • Promote collaboration across business, compliance, audit, and technology functions.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Risk Management, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree (MBA, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field) preferred.

Professional Certifications

Preferred certifications include:

  • Financial Risk Manager (FRM)
  • Professional Risk Manager (PRM)
  • Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
  • Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive banking and risk management experience.

raw.description:
Role: Actuarial Forecasting Lead

Duration: 12 months C2H

Location: Remote USA

Start Date: ASAP

Description:

12-15 years experienced Actuarial Forecasting Lead who understands claims behaviour, loss development and the financial performance of insurance and protection products. The person should be able to work closely with actuarial, finance and technology teams to strengthen claims projections, loss estimates and actuarial modelling capabilities.

Experience:

  • Strong experience in actuarial modelling, claims frequency and severity analysis, loss ratio projections and claims cost estimation.
  • Good understanding of extended warranty, device protection, service contracts or specialty insurance products.
  • Experience in claims reserving, loss development analysis and ultimate loss projections.
  • Hands on experience in building and reviewing actuarial models using historical claims experience, exposure data, product mix and cost assumptions.
  • Understanding of repair and replacement costs, claim incidence rates, product failure patterns and their impact on loss projections.
  • Experience with actuarial and analytical tools.
  • Exposure to statistical modelling, and AI ML techniques applied to claims and loss estimation.
  • Experience working with actuarial, claims, underwriting and finance teams.

Responsibilities:

  • Review existing actuarial forecasting models, methodologies and assumptions used to project warranty claims, device failures and replacement demand.
  • Analyse historical claims, failure rates, product behaviour, repair and replacement patterns to understand the factors influencing future claims volumes.
  • Assess the reliability of actuarial forecasts and identify gaps in modelling approaches, data quality and underlying assumptions.
  • Evaluate and recommend suitable statistical, actuarial and predictive modelling techniques to improve forecast accuracy.
  • Work with actuarial, supply chain, data science and engineering teams to improve forecasting models and ensure their outputs meet supply chain planning needs.
  • Validate forecast results through actual-versus-expected analysis, back-testing and scenario analysis.
  • Lead functional discussions, model validation, and business acceptance of the forecasting solution.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Actuarial Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related quantitative discipline.
  • Professional actuarial qualifications or progress towards actuarial certification would be an added advantage, but are not mandatory.
  • Practical experience in actuarial modelling, claims forecasting and applying actuarial projections to business planning is essential

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

raw.description:
Intuition Machines uses AI/ML to build enterprise security products. We apply our research to systems that serve hundreds of millions of people, with a team distributed around the world. You are probably familiar with our best-known product, the hCaptcha security suite. Our approach is simple: low overhead, small teams, and rapid iteration.

As a Senior Cybersecurity Fraud Analyst, you will use your expertise in data analysis, financial transactions, and web traffic analysis to identify and investigate potential fraudulent activities within our hCaptcha SaaS security platform.

Your primary responsibilities will include conducting advanced investigations into complex fraud patterns, developing actionable insights to enhance our fraud detection capabilities, and collaborating with machine learning teams to continuously improve our AI/ML detection and response systems.

Using AI: Coding agents are indisputably useful tools. We provide access to the top 3 models, and were early adopters of evals-first development flows. Familiarity with coding using agents is part of all interviews. However, reliability and correctness are critical for us. You will need to read and understand every line of code with your name on it, and it will be reviewed by both people and machines.


What will you do:

  • Monitor, identify, and analyze events from diverse data sources, including financial transactions and web traffic, to detect and respond to fraudulent activities.
  • Conduct advanced investigations of suspected fraud, analyzing behavior patterns and anomalies to assess risk and determine appropriate actions.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Engineering, Product, Customer Support, to enhance fraud detection and prevention strategies.
  • Help build and align fraud detection automation, dashboards, and reports.
  • Continuously audit and refine fraud detection measures to ensure compliance with industry standards and best practices.
  • Stay informed of emerging fraud trends, technologies, and regulatory changes to keep our fraud prevention strategies up-to-date.


What we are looking for:

  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in fraud detection, financial data analysis, risk management, or trust & safety.
  • Proficiency in SQL and ideally Python for data analysis and visualization.
  • In-depth understanding of fraud detection methodologies and the fraud landscape.
  • Ability to work with large datasets and derive actionable insights.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills, with a detail-oriented and analytical mindset.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills in English, able to work effectively across teams.
  • Familiarity with the analysis of web-based and API abuse.


Nice to Have:

  • Hands-on experience with web security and secure configuration practices.
  • Interest in staying current with industry trends and fraud prevention technologies.
  • Familiarity with modern fraud machine learning practices.
  • Holding a valid CFE, CFS, CFF, or CISA certification is a plus.


What do we offer:

  • Fully remote position with flexible working hours.
  • An inspiring team of colleagues spread all over the world.
  • Pleasant, modern development and deployment workflows: ship early, ship often.

About us

Implicity is a digital MedTech company delivering advanced innovation to cardiologists through Big Data and Artificial Intelligence.

Our industry-leading cardiac remote monitoring platform simplifies the management of complex clinical data and enables earlier identification of patient issues—helping clinicians deliver the right care at the right time.

In short, joining Implicity means contributing directly to improved patient outcomes.

Founded in 2016 by Dr. Arnaud Rosier, a cardiologist and AI researcher, and David Perlmutter, an engineer and entrepreneur, Implicity has grown into a transformative force in cardiac care.

More than a decade later, this French startup-turned-scale-up is helping shape the future of cardiology on a global scale.

  • Over 250 hospitals and medical centers already use Implicity’s solutions

  • Supporting more than 100,000 patients worldwide

    At Implicity, you’ll collaborate with experts across data science, engineering, clinical affairs, regulatory, IT, sales, and customer success, all working together toward a shared mission.

    The team has established Implicity as a clear European market leader and is now expanding rapidly in the U.S.

    Why Implicity?

  • Patients receive higher-quality, more proactive care

  • Physicians spend less time managing data and administrative burden, allowing greater focus on prevention and treatment

  • Healthcare payers benefit from lower overall costs by emphasizing monitoring and prevention over hospitalization and acute intervention

Job and recruitment context

The Customer Success Manager (CSM) - North America is responsible for ensuring the satisfaction, engagement, and retention of Implicity’s customers in the region. This role plays a crucial part in onboarding new clients, supporting them in scaling their remote cardiac monitoring activities, and serving as the primary point of contact for all customer needs.

Reporting to the Lead Customer Success Manager, the CSM will collaborate closely with sales, product, and clinical teams to drive customer success and influence product development based on customer feedback.

Working closely with the Lead Customer Success Manager and the US Sales team, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Customer Onboarding & Training: Manage the entire onboarding process for new clients, ensuring they are set up for success and trained effectively on Implicity’s remote monitoring platform.

  • Customer Relationship Management: Foster and maintain strong relationships with clients, providing ongoing support and guidance to help them scale their remote patient monitoring programs.

  • Technical Support & Issue Resolution: Address customer inquiries, troubleshoot technical issues, and coordinate with internal teams to ensure timely resolution.

  • Process Improvement & Best Practices: Develop and implement best practices, playbooks, and standardized procedures for onboarding and customer engagement.

  • Customer Education & Communication: Serve as the primary liaison between customers and Implicity’s internal teams, keeping customers informed about platform updates, new features, and best practices.

  • Project Management: Lead and manage customer-specific projects, such as EHR integrations and workflow optimizations, to enhance the overall customer experience.

Education

  • Prior experience in remote cardiac monitoring or cardiology-related technology is highly preferred.

  • Experience managing complex projects and cross-functional teams.

  • Proficiency in using CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce, Airtable) and collaboration tools (e.g., Slack, Notion).

Skills/Aptitude

  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently.

  • Exceptional ability to build relationships with clinical professionals and administrative stakeholders.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

  • High attention to detail, analytical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities.

  • Passion for customer success and a deep understanding of customer engagement strategies

  • Willingness to travel as needed to support customer success initiatives.

1° Screening interview (either HR or Manager)

2° Job interview with Krissy (Lead Customer Success US), your future manager

4° Possible reference check and background check

Job Description:

Data Governance Analyst

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact supporting the Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program. The CMM program is an initiative to support the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AO) in developing a modern cloud-based solution to support all 204+ federal courts across the United States.

GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career. The Data Governance Analyst will be part of the CMM Data Modernization and Governance team responsible for delivering an integrated data governance, engineering, data platform, reporting, analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities that support operational decision-making and fulfill AO's data and analytics objectives in support of the CMM program.

The successful candidate will be responsible for establishing, implementing, and maintaining the organization's data governance framework so that data is managed and protected as a strategic enterprise asset and to accelerate CMM modernization efforts. This role acts as a Data Standards Architect, defining and documenting data standards, definitions, and structures across systems, and works closely with legal, compliance, security, and business stakeholders to ensure data is handled in accordance with privacy, security, retention, classification, and regulatory requirements. This role also ensures alignment with Judiciary policies, practices, and the current Data Governance Roadmap, and fosters a data driven culture across the AO and local courts.

The Data Governance Analyst will execute the following responsibilities:

  • Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of the CMM Data Governance framework, policies, standards, procedures, and operating models.
  • Serve as a Data Standards Architect, define, document, and maintain data standards, naming conventions, data definitions, data structures, reference data, and governance requirements.
  • Develop and maintain data governance standards aligned with enterprise architecture, security, privacy, records management, and regulatory requirements.
  • Establish and maintain data ownership, stewardship, accountability, and decision-rights models.
  • Partner with Data Stewards, Data Owners, business stakeholders, security, privacy, legal, records management, and technology teams to operationalize governance requirements.
  • Ensure data assets are appropriately classified and managed based on sensitivity, criticality, and business value.
  • Support compliance with data privacy, security, retention, classification, records management, and regulatory requirements.
  • Translate policies and regulatory requirements into actionable data governance controls and procedures.
  • Identify governance gaps, risks, and areas of non-compliance and coordinate remediation activities.
  • Support data access, sharing, usage, and lifecycle governance processes.
  • Participate in governance councils, working groups, and data domain forums.
  • Develop governance documentation, standards, procedures, decision logs, and supporting artifacts.
  • Monitor adoption and effectiveness of governance policies and standards.
  • Support governance-related assessments, audits, and compliance reviews.
  • Contribute to the development of data governance roadmaps, maturity assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Support the data stewardship program by defining data ownership roles, responsibilities, and RACI models across business and technical teams.
  • Develop training materials and deliver awareness sessions on data governance policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.
  • Track, analyze, and report data governance program metrics, maturity, and compliance status to leadership and governance councils.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MA/MS degree with 5+ years of general experience in information systems and 7+ years of specialized experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in supporting enterprise data governance programs.
  • Experience translating governance policy into practical operational processes in delivery environments.
  • Strong understanding of data quality management, metadata practices, and stewardship models.
  • Experience governing high-sensitivity or regulated data with clear compliance expectations.
  • Experience with data quality profiling and monitoring techniques and common tooling patterns.
  • Experience defining and governing enterprise data standards across multiple teams and delivery pods.
  • Strong background in data modeling, integration patterns, and change data capture concepts.
  • Experience with metadata and catalog tools such as Collibra, Alation, or Qlik.
  • Practical experience implementing glossary and lineage capabilities in modern data platforms.
  • Ability to translate technical metadata into business-friendly definitions and documentation.
  • Experience implementing data privacy controls in regulated or high-sensitivity environments.
  • Experience with access management and operationalizing privacy requirements.
  • Experience partnering with security, governance, and engineering teams to implement compliant data sharing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in Federal Government or regulated environments.
  • Experience with enterprise data governance frameworks and operating models.
  • Data management certification.

raw.description:
Join a global Contract Resource Organization (CRO) where innovation meets purpose. At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we're driven by a shared commitment to improving lives through high-quality clinical research. Our teams are empowered to think creatively, take ownership, and deliver meaningful work that helps bring life-changing therapies to patients around the world.


With more than 4,000 professionals across the globe, we foster a collaborative and inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, growth is encouraged, and every contribution makes an impact. Whether you're building your career or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and help shape the future of clinical research.


Make an Impact as a In-House Clinical Research Associate at Worldwide


Help keep clinical studies moving forward by supporting effective site management throughout the study lifecycle. In this role, you’ll work closely with Clinical Trial Managers, field Clinical Research Associates, study sites, and cross-functional project teams to help deliver site activities accurately and on schedule.

You’ll have broad involvement across site management, from study start-up and essential documentation through remote monitoring, data review, recruitment support, and study close-out. Your work will help sites stay prepared, informed, and aligned with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), applicable regulations, and study requirements.


Where You'll Work

This is a remote role open to candidates based in Argentina or Brazil. You will collaborate with global teams across multiple time zones.


What You'll Do

  • Support site management activities throughout the study lifecycle, including feasibility, study initiation, interim and remote monitoring, and close-out activities under appropriate guidance.
  • Maintain regular communication with assigned sites and partner with Clinical Trial Managers and field CRAs to keep study activities and deliverables on track.
  • Review site documentation for quality and completeness, support Trial Master File (TMF) filing and reconciliation, and help maintain Investigator Site Files (ISFs).
  • Review electronic data capture (EDC) records for completion, logic, and compliance, and assist sites with resolving data management and vendor queries.
  • Prepare CRAs for site visits by tracking and communicating action items, protocol deviations, outstanding queries, study supplies, training, and other open activities.
  • Coordinate study materials, support site staff changes and system access, and help ensure required training, qualifications, delegation, and regulatory documentation remain current.
  • Support site prescreening, screening, recruitment, and Subject Eligibility Review tracking, as applicable to the study.
  • Maintain study trackers, pull information from study-specific portals and systems, and provide timely updates to Clinical Trial Managers and project teams.
  • Serve as a key operational contact for clinical research activities when appropriate, helping sites and study teams address issues and maintain progress.

What You'll Bring

  • A four-year college curriculum with a major concentration in medical, biological, physical, health, pharmacy, or another related science is preferred; alternatively, a two-year college curriculum or equivalent education/training plus at least one year of relevant clinical research experience, or other relevant education/training plus at least two years of clinical research experience, may be considered.
  • A basic understanding of clinical research principles and processes, with knowledge of applicable FDA and/or EU regulations, ICH Guidelines, local regulatory requirements, and standard operating procedures.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the interpersonal skills to work effectively with sites and cross-functional study teams.
  • Good planning, organization, and time-management skills, with a methodical approach to managing multiple activities.
  • Basic knowledge of Microsoft Office and familiarity with IVRS and electronic CRF systems.
  • Proficiency in spoken and written English + Spanish + Portuguese along with fluency in the local languages of the countries under your responsibility.

Discover the Difference


We love knowing that someone is going to have a better life because of the work we do.  Discover the Difference at Worldwide Clinical Trials. Explore additional opportunities on our careers page, visit , or connect with us onLinkedIn.

raw.description:
Position:

Senior Corporate Auditor

Job Description:

Arrow Corporate Audit’s mission is to deliver responsive risk-based audit and advisory services in a spirit of partnership with objectivity, fairness, transparency, and in accordance with our professional and ethical standards to our stakeholders. This role in instrumental in achieving that mission.

This role sits within the rapidly expanding EMEA Corporate Audit Team and is primarily based in London, although audit engagements and projects will be executed throughout the EMEA region.


Senior Auditors are a crucial business partner to Arrow businesses, departments and other key stakeholders. They execute high quality, value-adding projects in a managed, professional, detailed, diligent and collegiate manner. They are credible and are able to communicate complicated issues and the concept of risk and risk management to non-finance based individuals as well as senior executives and business leaders throughout the Arrow organization.

Our Senior Auditors are the team captains and are charged with leading delivery of our audit and advisory services across our global organization address all areas of enterprise risk management (strategic, financial, operational, compliance, and reputational) and establishing the team culture. They demonstrate thorough knowledge and a proven record of success in completing aspects of the Internal Audit process, control evaluation and testing methodologies, and other Financial and Operational Internal Control methodologies and terminology e.g. COSO.

Arrow Senior Auditors are agile thinkers and are able to react, adjust their project scope and procedures and problem solve where required. They are able to see the wider-risk and form an opinion on the level to which it is mitigated. They are able to execute a bespoke engagement to deliver specific assurance on a stated goal and they do not rely on thoughtlessly executing a standard, repetitive work-program. Consequently, Arrow Senior Auditors are a highly prized team-member, whose experiences, feedback and input are invaluable to the function as it seeks to constantly evolve, improve and provide gold standard audit projects to the business.


What will you be doing at Arrow?

  • Leading teams, emphasizing the supervising of staff by creating a positive working environment through the building of solid relationships with team members; the monitoring of workloads of all team members; adjustment and redistribution of assignments accordingly to promote work/life quality, the taking into account of team members capabilities and needs and meeting of business partner expectations; encouragement of team dialogue; the providing of candid, meaningful feedback in a timely manner; and the keeping of team members and leadership informed on progress and issues.
  • Using available technical resources and tools to research and expand one's sphere of knowledge to enhance work product, and to remain up to date on hot topics affecting Arrow's business and industry while sharing the knowledge with the team where applicable.
  • Collaborating directly with key stakeholders in the organization, identifying and addressing needs through building solid relationships with stakeholders; understanding the Company’s business; and actively participating in discussions and meetings.
  • Managing day-to-day engagement operations, including preparing concise, accurate documents and addressing unanticipated issues; demonstrating flexibility in prioritizing and completing tasks; and communicating potential conflicts to leadership.
  • Develop and or review audit programs, benchmark financial and operational processes as well as perform process optimization.
  • Creating high quality deliverable using appropriate business and technical language, especially developing and reviewing audit programs or testing steps, adapting an audit program to suit a specific environment, and/or designing special projects evaluation and testing work plans.
  • Involved with and contributing to specific company wide strategies and initiatives.

What are we looking for?

  • At least 4/5 years audit or consulting experience preferably in Manufacturing, Distribution/ Supply Chain Industry.
  • Education background: CPA/ ACA/ CIA/ CMA or MBA preferred.
  • Business Fluency in English language.
  • Willingness to travel internationally up to 25% of the time. The team meets in London twice per month.
  • Experience of working in Big 4 companies preferred.
  • Strong skills in Microsoft tools especially in Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Data Analytics and AI (ACL, Power BI, Copilot Pro (preferred), Claude, etc.).
  • Exposure to Oracle, AX, or similar systems.

What is in it for you?

  • Competitive and attractive employee compensation package.
  • Benefits
  • Reliable & trusting work environment.
  • Cooperative team with flat structures and communication.
  • Professional and personal development.
  • Work Shift: Full Time 37.5hrs Monday- Friday 9.00am-5.30pm (30 mins lunch)
  • Remote working

Do you see yourself as our future colleague? If yes - send us your application.

raw.description:
AHEAD builds platforms for digital business. By weaving together advances in cloud infrastructure, automation and analytics, and software delivery, we help enterprises deliver on the promise of digital transformation.
At AHEAD, we prioritize creating a culture of belonging, where all perspectives and voices are represented, valued, respected, and heard. We create spaces to empower everyone to speak up, make change, and drive the culture at AHEAD.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and do not discriminate based on an individual's race, national origin, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, marital status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law, whether actual or perceived.
We embrace all candidates that will contribute to the diversification and enrichment of ideas and perspectives at AHEAD.

The Technical Program Manager leads complex, multi-workstream technology programs that span related projects and teams across the lifecycle of an engagement. This role is accountable for working with cross-functional teams on aligning customer outcomes, solution strategy, commercial commitments, integrated delivery plans, and execution across AHEAD.

The Technical Program Manager operates at the intersection of Pre-Sales, Sales, Delivery, Practices, Resource Management, Finance, partners, and customer leadership. They help shape opportunities, establish the program operating model, coordinate project and workstream leaders, manage cross-project dependencies and financial outcomes, and provide the executive visibility required to make timely decisions and realize value.

Duties and Responsibilities:

    Program Strategy, Opportunity Shaping, and Commercial Planning

    • Lead program-level shaping of complex lifecycle management programs in partnership with Pre-Sales, Sales, Architects, Technical Leads, Practice leaders, and customer stakeholders.
    • Translate a strategic customer objective into an integrated program structure of related projects, workstreams, milestones, outcomes, dependencies, and decision points.
    • Develop and validate program assumptions, schedules, delivery approach, staffing strategy and resources forecasting, labor mix, schedule, partner or vendor inputs, and pricing recommendations with the appropriate stakeholders.
    • Assess delivery feasibility, challenge solution and schedule assumptions, identify cross-workstream risks, and surface tradeoffs before commitments are made to the customer.
    • Support proposals, solution reviews, statements of work, estimates, executive presentations, and internal approvals with practical program-level content.
    • Ensure a disciplined transition from opportunity shaping to delivery so that scope, assumptions, commercial commitments, risks, and decisions are understood across the program team.

      • Program Mobilization and Operating Model

      • Collaborate with the PMO to establish the program charter, integrated master plan, and shared governance model, in alignment with established program frameworks. This includes roles and decision rights, stakeholder alignment on priorities and outcomes, mutual accountability, communication plan, escalation paths, reporting dashboards and cadence, and RAID framework.
      • Collaborate with resource management and delivery leaders to forecast resources (internal or third party) as well as align project managers, workstream leads, technical teams, partners, and customer stakeholders around shared outcomes, sequencing, interdependencies, and measures of success.
      • Confirm readiness across staffing, customer access, environments, procurement, vendor coordination, technical prerequisites, operational requirements, and required approvals.
      • Define program-level standards for status reporting, dependency management, risk escalation, change control, quality, acceptance, and decision documentation.
      • Establish program KPIs and dashboards that provide an accurate view of progress, health, financial performance, risks, dependencies, and value realization.
      • Coach and support project managers and workstream leads in applying effective delivery practices while maintaining accountability for integrated program outcomes.

        • Multi-Workstream Technical Delivery and Lifecycle Management

        • Lead execution of large lifecycle management programs across infrastructure, cloud, network, security, platform, data center, or related technology environments.
        • Coordinate multiple projects, technical workstreams, delivery teams, partners, and vendors with complex interdependencies and shared milestones.
        • Partner with Architects and Technical Leads to sequence work, resolve cross-workstream constraints, validate technical decisions, and maintain alignment to the approved solution and customer outcomes.
        • Manage the integrated schedule and critical path, ensuring that project-level plans roll up to a coherent program plan and that impacts are understood across workstreams.
        • Track delivery against scope, schedule, budget, quality, acceptance criteria, and program outcomes; drive corrective action when performance deviates from plan.
        • Manage the relationship between program commitments and lifecycle operations, including implementation, knowledge transfer, transition to run or managed services, and post-go-live stabilization.
        • Assess the current technical environment and operational processes to define tactical and strategic initiatives that enhance service delivery and continuously improve the overall program approach.
        • Maintain visibility into systemic impediments and resolve or escalate issues that cannot be addressed within an individual project or workstream.

          • Program Governance, Financial Management, and Controls

          • Own program governance and provide transparent reporting on overall health, scope, schedule, financial performance, resources, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and customer outcomes.
          • Manage program financials, including labor burn, forecast, estimate-to-complete, revenue or billing milestones, gross margin drivers, invoicing readiness, and variance across projects and workstreams.
          • Control program scope through documented change management, evaluating impacts to schedule, resources, pricing, commercial terms, interdependencies, and value realization before changes are approved.
          • Coordinate vendor and partner performance, commercial obligations, dependencies, and escalations across the program.
          • Ensure program execution follows applicable contractual, security, quality, compliance, and operational requirements.
          • Use dashboards, KPIs, and data-driven insights to identify trends, improve predictability, and focus leadership attention on the most important decisions.
          • Identify patterns that may affect profitability, utilization, customer satisfaction, delivery quality, or future lifecycle opportunities and engage the right leaders early.

            • Executive Stakeholder Leadership and Communication

            • Build trusted relationships with customer sponsors, executive stakeholders, Sales, Pre-Sales, Delivery, Practice leaders, technical teams, vendors, and shared services.
            • Translate complex technical and commercial information into concise, audience-appropriate communication that supports alignment, decision-making, and executive action.
            • Provide regular executive reporting that clearly communicates progress, outcomes, upcoming milestones, decisions required, risks, emerging issues, dependencies, business impacts, recommended actions, and recovery plans. Manage the communication of difficult news and delivery challenges promptly and transparently.
            • Lead program business reviews, both internal and with clients, to highlight accomplishments, evaluate performance, review key metrics, demonstrate value and ROI, identify risks and gaps, and align on goals for the upcoming quarter.
            • Facilitate program steering committees, executive checkpoints, cross-workstream decisions, and escalation forums with clear objectives and documented outcomes. Lead complex program decisions by evaluating trade-offs, aligning stakeholders, and driving timely resolution of issues within established decision authority.
            • Set expectations, manage tradeoffs, and influence without formal authority while protecting the customer relationship and AHEAD commitments.
            • Represent AHEAD with professionalism, sound judgment, customer focus, and a commitment to delivering measurable business and technical value.

              • Program Risk, Issue, Dependency, and Change Leadership

              • Operate effectively in high-ambiguity environments, navigating shifting priorities with flexibility and making timely decisions with incomplete information. Adapt program strategies to maintain resilience, delivery continuity, and alignment with business objectives while escalating material risks appropriately.
              • Maintain an active program-level risk, issue, and problem management process, assigning owners, due dates, mitigation actions, escalation paths, and resolution criteria. Partner with incident, change, and problem management experts to drive proactive resolution and reduce risk.
              • Identify risks created by interdependencies, sequencing, resource constraints, technical complexity, vendor performance, commercial terms, or organizational change.
              • Lead integrated recovery planning when programs are off track, aligning stakeholders on options, tradeoffs, corrective actions, and revised commitments.
              • Coordinate program-level changes and ensure impacts are communicated consistently across projects, workstreams, customer stakeholders, and internal leadership.
              • Surface systemic delivery gaps and recommend improvements to program methods, handoffs, tools, governance, and organizational practices.

                • Transition, Value Realization, and Continuous Improvement

                • Lead program closeout and value-realization activities, including acceptance, financial reconciliation, benefits tracking, documentation, customer feedback, lessons learned, and administrative completion.
                • Ensure the customer and operational teams are prepared for transition, support, lifecycle operations, warranty, managed services, or ongoing improvement activities as applicable.
                • Capture and apply lessons learned across projects and workstreams to improve estimating, scoping, handoffs, and delivery practices. Develop repeatable processes, templates, and governance artifacts to standardize execution, institutionalize improvements, and support scalable program delivery.
                • Partner with Sales, Pre-Sales, and Delivery to identify follow-on needs, expansion opportunities, and lifecycle considerations without compromising program integrity.
                • Contribute to the maturity of AHEAD program management standards, technical delivery practices, tools, playbooks, and quality controls.

Education & Experience:

    Minimum Required

    • Bachelor’s degree in project management, business, engineering, information technology, or a related field; equivalent experience considered.
    • 8+ years of experience leading complex technology projects, programs, or multi-workstream initiatives in professional services, consulting, systems integration, managed services, or a related technology environment.
    • Demonstrated experience in directly leading large, complex programs from opportunity shaping and solution definition through execution, transition, and value realization.
    • Experience directly coordinating multiple related projects, technical workstreams, delivery teams, vendors, and stakeholders with complex interdependencies.
    • Experience partnering with Pre-Sales and Sales to develop program scope, estimates, staffing models, pricing inputs, statements of work, and delivery assumptions.
    • Strong understanding of program financial management, including budget, forecast, labor utilization, margin drivers, change control, revenue or billing milestones, and estimate-to-complete.
    • Technical fluency across enterprise infrastructure, cloud, networking, security, platforms, data center, or related lifecycle management services, with the ability to lead technical discussions without needing to be the solution architect or hands-on engineer.
    • Proven ability to establish program governance, integrated plans, executive reporting, risk and issue management, dependency management, and decision processes.
    • Experience coaching or guiding project managers, workstream leads, technical leads, or cross-functional delivery teams.
    • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and executive communication skills.
    • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, and influence outcomes without direct authority.

      • Preferred

      • 10+ years of experience leading large, multi-million-dollar technology programs, ideally in a professional services, systems integration, consulting, or managed services environment.
      • PMP, PgMP, PMI-ACP, PRINCE2, or comparable project or program management certification.
      • ITIL certification or practical experience with service transition, operational readiness, and IT service management practices.
      • Experience with commercial contracts, statements of work, change orders, vendor management, and customer negotiations.
      • Experience using professional services automation, financial, resource management, project portfolio, and reporting tools.
      • Cloud, infrastructure, networking, security, or other relevant technical certifications.
      • Experience leading multi-year transformation, modernization, migration, or lifecycle management programs across multiple practices or delivery organizations.
      • Experience applying Agile, hybrid, or other scaled delivery approaches across multiple teams or workstreams.

Competencies:

    • Strategic and systems thinking across interconnected projects, workstreams, stakeholders, and outcomes
    • Program leadership, integrated planning, and execution discipline
    • Technical fluency and the ability to connect architecture, delivery, operations, and business value
    • Commercial and financial acumen
    • Executive presence, concise communication, and effective facilitation
    • Risk-based thinking, decision-making, and recovery leadership
    • Cross-functional collaboration and influence without formal authority
    • Coaching mindset and ability to develop project and workstream leaders
    • Customer focus and commitment to measurable outcomes
    • Adaptability, comfort with ambiguity, and a bias to action
    • Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on quality, predictability, profitability, and scalable delivery
The compensation range indicated in this posting reflects the On-Target Earnings (“OTE”) for this role, which includes a base salary and any applicable target bonus amount. This OTE range may vary based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and geographic location.

Why AHEAD:

Through our daily work and internal groups like Moving Women AHEAD and RISE AHEAD, we value and benefit from diversity of people, ideas, experience, and everything in between.
We fuel growth by stacking our office with top-notch technologies in a multi-million-dollar lab, by encouraging cross department training and development, sponsoring certifications and credentials for continued learning.

About the Role

Turner & Townsend is seeking an experienced Change Management Manager to support the successful delivery of organizational transformation initiatives across our financial services client's facility construction programs and projects. The successful candidate will lead the development and execution of change management strategies that drive stakeholder engagement, business readiness, user adoption, and sustainable outcomes.

The ideal candidate will possess strong experience in commercial construction project management, organizational change management, business transformation, stakeholder engagement, communications, and adoption planning. This role requires close collaboration with project teams, business leaders, and key stakeholders to ensure the people side of change is effectively managed and aligned with project objectives.

As a key member of the Program Management Office, the Change Management Manager will help navigate delivery partner integration, ensure workstream cohesion, and achieve business objectives while promoting Turner & Townsend's values, methodologies, and commitment to delivering better outcomes.

What you'll do

Lead the development and execution of change management strategies, plans, and initiatives to support organizational transformation across multiple workstreams.

Engage and influence executive sponsors, project teams, and stakeholders to build alignment and drive successful change outcomes.

Conduct stakeholder assessments, change impact assessments, organizational readiness evaluations, and adoption planning activities.

Bring retail and corporate banking construction industry insight and best practices to shape the transformation agenda and ensure a consistent and repeatable change management approach is embedded across multiple service providers.

Develop and implement communication, engagement, and business readiness strategies to support project objectives.

Partner with leadership teams to identify change risks, opportunities, and mitigation strategies.

Design and deliver change management materials, presentations, workshops, and stakeholder engagement activities.

Monitor adoption, readiness, and benefits realization metrics to measure the effectiveness of change initiatives.

Support business process improvements and transformation initiatives through analysis and continuous improvement activities.

Facilitate workshops, focus groups, training sessions, and stakeholder meetings to drive awareness and engagement.

Collaborate with communications, training, project management, and business teams to ensure an integrated delivery approach.

Develop and maintain stakeholder management plans, communication plans, and change roadmaps.

Support user acceptance testing, operational readiness, and transition activities for new processes, systems, and technologies.

Manage multiple change initiatives simultaneously while ensuring alignment with project schedules and business priorities.

Prepare executive-level reporting, dashboards, and change performance updates for key stakeholders.

Promote knowledge sharing, lessons learned, and continuous improvement across programs and projects.

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Organizational Development, Communications, Project Management, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of experience in organizational change management, business transformation, program management, or related disciplines.
  • Experience with construction project management programs. Experience with financial services client facility construction desired.
  • Proven experience supporting large-scale transformation, technology implementation, or business process improvement initiatives.
  • Experience conducting stakeholder analysis, change impact assessments, readiness assessments, and adoption planning.
  • Experience developing executive communications, training materials, and engagement strategies.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all organizational levels.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Prosci Change Management Certification, PMP, or equivalent certification preferred.

*SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs*

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.

We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this, we promote a healthy, productive, and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

Turner & Townsend is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.

Please find out more about us at www.turnerandtownsend.com/ and

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Twitter

Instagram

LinkedIn

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives.
